answer: To counter Sybil attacks, networks enforce a quadratic stake-slashing mechanism that penalizes clustered identities. Burning deposits creates economic friction: when malicious replicas multiply, their registration cost follows a superlinear spiral $O(n^2)$. Sybil clusters hit a profitability nadir as their operational capital vanishes into an unrecoverable burn lagoon, making large-scale coordination mathematically prohibitive.
